stories.headline: Xiaomi Releases MiMo-V2.5-Pro, a 1T-Parameter Open-Weight Model Rivaling Claude Opus on Coding

key_facts.fact: MiMo-V2.5-Pro is a mixture-of-experts model with 1.02 trillion total parameters and 42 billion active per request, with a 1 million token context window.
key_facts.excerpt: It packs 1.02 trillion total parameters, with 42 billion active per request. The MiMo team built this version specifically for jobs that run for hours and rack up thousands of tool calls.

key_facts.fact: The model built a complete compiler from a Peking University course in 4.3 hours across 672 tool calls, scoring 233 out of 233 on the hidden test suite.
key_facts.excerpt: MiMo-V2.5-Pro finished the project in 4.3 hours across 672 tool calls, scoring 233 out of 233 on the hidden test suite.

key_facts.fact: On SWE-bench Verified it scores 78.9%, on SWE-Bench Pro 57.2%, and on Terminal-Bench 2.0 68.4%, placing it close to Claude Opus 4.6 (77.1 on MiMo Coding Bench).
key_facts.excerpt: the model scores 78.9 on SWE-bench Verified, 57.2 on SWE-Bench Pro, and 68.4 on Terminal-Bench 2.0. On Xiaomi's in-house MiMo Coding Bench, it scores 73.7, putting it close to Claude Opus 4.6 (77.1)

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi claims MiMo-V2.5-Pro uses 40 to 60 percent fewer tokens than Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4 on equivalent agent tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: That's 40 to 60 percent fewer tokens than Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4 need to reach similar numbers, according to the team.

key_facts.fact: In a second demo, MiMo-V2.5-Pro wrote a desktop video editor with roughly 8,000 lines of code running autonomously for 11.5 hours and making about 1,870 tool calls.
key_facts.excerpt: MiMo-V2.5-Pro wrote a desktop video editor with roughly 8,000 lines of code from just a few prompts. The model ran autonomously for 11.5 hours and made about 1,870 tool calls.

sources.title: Xiaomi's open-weight MiMo-V2.5-Pro takes aim at Claude Opus with hours-long autonomous coding

stories.headline: Anthropic Finalizes $1.5B Joint Venture With Blackstone, Goldman Sachs to Sell AI to PE Portfolios

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is finalizing an approximately $1.5 billion joint venture with Blackstone, Goldman Sachs, Hellman & Friedman, and General Atlantic to sell AI tools to private-equity-backed companies.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic was finalising an approximately $1.5bn joint venture with a small group of Wall Street firms, with an announcement expected as soon as Monday.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic, Blackstone, and Hellman & Friedman are each expected to invest roughly $300 million; Goldman Sachs is set to invest around $150 million as a founding investor.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic, Blackstone and Hellman & Friedman are anchoring the deal, and each company is expected to invest roughly $300 million... Goldman Sachs is also set to be a founding investor, putting in around $150 million.

key_facts.fact: The venture will operate as a consulting and deployment arm, helping PE portfolio companies integrate Claude across operations in areas like finance, customer service, and analytics.
key_facts.excerpt: The investors will create a vehicle that operates as something between a consulting arm and a deployment factory: helping the portfolio companies of its private-equity backers integrate Claude across their day-to-day operations.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced a similar but larger joint venture, DeployCo, anchored by TPG, Bain Capital, Advent International, Brookfield, and Goanna Capital with about $4 billion committed.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI announced a similar joint venture, DeployCo, last month, anchored by TPG, Bain Capital, Advent International, Brookfield, and Goanna Capital. The five PE firms together committed about $4bn.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs has been piloting Claude internally for autonomous agents in accounting and compliance, with embedded Anthropic engineers reportedly spending six months inside the bank.
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman Sachs has spent the past several months piloting Claude internally as the basis for autonomous agents in accounting and compliance, with embedded Anthropic engineers reportedly spending six months inside the bank co-developing the systems.

stories.headline: Cerebras Targets Up to $40B Valuation in IPO, Kicks Off Roadshow Monday

key_facts.excerpt: AI chipmaker Cerebras Systems, a rival to Nvidia, is scheduled to kick off its IPO roadshow on Monday, with shares expected to be priced between $115 and $125... The company now aims to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol 'CBRS'.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported Cerebras could raise up to $4 billion, targeting a valuation of around $40 billion, making it one of the largest AI chip listings to date.
key_facts.excerpt: According to a Bloomberg News report last week, Cerebras could raise up to $4 billion, targeting a valuation of around $40 billion.

key_facts.fact: Cerebras revenue rose to $510 million in 2025, up from $290.3 million the prior year, and reported profit of $1.38 per share, a turnaround from a loss of $9.90 per share.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang Says Nvidia's China AI Chip Market Share Has Dropped to Zero

key_facts.fact: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the company's market share of AI accelerators in China has 'now dropped to zero' in an interview with the Special Competitive Studies Project (SCSP).
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that the company's market share of AI accelerators in China has now dropped to 0%.

key_facts.fact: Huang said US export policy 'has already largely backfired' and that abandoning a market the size of China is strategically unwise.
key_facts.excerpt: US export restrictions bite. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that the company's market share of AI accelerators in China has now dropped to 0%.

key_facts.fact: Bernstein earlier predicted Nvidia's China AI GPU share could fall from 66% in 2024 to about 8%; the actual decline to zero was far steeper than expected.
key_facts.excerpt: Bernstein had predicted Nvidia's China AI GPU market share could fall from 66% in 2024 to about 8% in the coming years, but the decline was far more dramatic according to Huang.

key_facts.fact: Some estimates suggest roughly $1 billion worth of Nvidia chips are being smuggled into China per quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Some estimates are that a billion dollars worth of Nvidia chips are being smuggled into China per quarter

key_facts.fact: Huang acknowledged China remains a formidable AI competitor even without advanced US GPUs, citing its cheaper energy, massive talent pool of scientists and mathematicians, and growing domestic hardware alternatives.
key_facts.excerpt: Even without advanced AI GPUs and the US software stack, China remains a formidable competitor in frontier AI models. China has cheaper energy, incredible talent, and an enormous number of scientists and mathematicians.

stories.headline: Five Eyes Intelligence Alliance Publishes Joint Guidance Warning Against Rapid Agentic AI Adoption

key_facts.fact: CISA, NSA, and cybersecurity agencies from the UK, Australia, Canada, and New Zealand co-authored guidance titled 'Careful adoption of agentic AI services' published on Friday May 2.
key_facts.excerpt: The agencies delivered that position last Friday in a guide titled Careful adoption of agentic AI services [PDF]

key_facts.fact: The document lists 23 different risks and over 100 individual best practices, warning that every component in an agentic AI system widens the attack surface.
key_facts.excerpt: The document contains more scary stories, then lists 23 different risks and over 100 individual best practices to address them.

key_facts.fact: The agencies warn organizations should 'assume that agentic AI systems may behave unexpectedly' and prioritize 'resilience, reversibility and risk containment over efficiency gains.'
key_facts.excerpt: Until security practices, evaluation methods and standards mature, organisations should assume that agentic AI systems may behave unexpectedly and plan deployments accordingly, prioritizing resilience, reversibility and risk containment over efficiency gains.

key_facts.fact: The guidance recommends organizations should 'never grant broad or unrestricted access, especially to sensitive data' and 'only use agentic AI for low-risk and non-sensitive tasks.'
key_facts.excerpt: Safely using AI agents means 'never granting it broad or unrestricted access, especially to sensitive data or critical systems,' the document warns. Companies, it says, 'should only use agentic AI for low-risk and non-sensitive tasks.'

key_facts.fact: The agencies note that threat intelligence for agentic AI is still evolving, with OWASP and MITRE ATLAS currently focused on LLMs, leaving some attack vectors unique to agentic AI unaddressed.
key_facts.excerpt: Threat intelligence for agentic AI systems is still evolving... resources like the Open Web Application Security Project and MITRE ATLAS currently focus on LLMs. As a result, some attack vectors unique to agentic AI may not be fully captured or addressed.

sources.title: Five Eyes spook shops warn rapid rollouts of agentic AI are too risky
US and allies urge 'careful adoption' of AI agents

stories.headline: xAI Quietly Releases Grok 4.3 With Always-On Reasoning and $1.25/M Token Pricing

key_facts.fact: xAI released Grok 4.3 quietly with no press release, featuring always-on reasoning that cannot be toggled off, a 1M-token context window, and uncapped output length.
key_facts.excerpt: xAI dropped Grok 4.3 quietly — no press release, just a new entry in the model selector... Always-on reasoning, no knobs. Unlike most reasoning models, you can't dial the effort up or down — reasoning is always active.

key_facts.fact: Grok 4.3 is priced at $1.25/$2.50 per million input/output tokens, reducing overall running costs by approximately 20% compared to Grok 4.20 according to Artificial Analysis estimates.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial Analysis estimates that Grok 4.3 reduces overall running costs by approximately 20% compared to Grok 4.20.

key_facts.fact: The model matches the scale of Grok 4.20 including its 16-agent Heavy system, with an improved architecture and a December 2025 knowledge cutoff.
key_facts.excerpt: Grok 4.3 is a new pre-trained model matching the scale of Grok 4.20 with an improved architecture and a December 2025 knowledge cutoff.

key_facts.fact: The model adds native video understanding and the ability to generate structured documents like slides, PDFs, and spreadsheets directly in conversation.
key_facts.excerpt: The new model carries over the architecture from Grok 4.20, including the 16-agent Heavy system and a large context window, while adding native video understanding, sharper reasoning from extended training runs, and the ability to generate structured documents — slides, PDFs, spreadsheets — directly in conversation.

key_facts.fact: On the Intelligence Index, Grok 4.3 now sits just above Muse Spark and Claude Sonnet 4.6.
key_facts.excerpt: it now sits just above Muse Spark and Claude Sonnet 4.6 on the Intelligence Index.

sources.title: Grok 4.3 Is Live in Kilo Code

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Security Public Beta for Enterprise Vulnerability Scanning

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced the public beta of Claude Security, a cybersecurity tool that scans codebases, detects vulnerabilities, and generates patches, powered by Claude Opus 4.7.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has announced the public beta for Claude Security, its cybersecurity tool used for scanning codebases, detecting vulnerabilities, and generating patches.

key_facts.fact: Claude Security can scan full enterprise repositories and open Claude Code to fix vulnerabilities in a single session, with one-click scanning that analyzes component relationships and data usage.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Security can scan full enterprise repositories to flag potential flaws – then open Claude Code to fix them – to reduce detection and response to one session for cyber workers.

key_facts.fact: The tool attaches a confidence percentage to each finding to reduce false positives, and now includes scheduled and targeted scans plus export to Slack, Jira, CSV, and Markdown.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic tweaked the tool to place a greater emphasis on validating AI findings, attaching a confidence percentage to each finding to reduce false positives. New additions also include scheduled and targeted scans, as well as the option to export findings to Slack, Jira, or as CSV and Markdown files.

key_facts.fact: Claude Security was previously known as Claude Code Security, first made available to select organizations as a research preview; it is now accessible within Claude or via a dedicated website page.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Security was previously known as Claude Code Security, which Anthropic first made available to select organizations as a research preview... Claude Security is accessible directly within Claude, or via a dedicated page on its website.

key_facts.fact: The launch follows the UK AI Security Institute's independent verification that Anthropic's Mythos Preview was the first model to complete a 32-step enterprise network attack simulation.
key_facts.excerpt: The UK's AI Security Institute (AISI) has independently verified that the model is more capable at cyber tasks, and that it was the first to complete a 32-step enterprise network attack simulation designed to test LLM cyber exploit capabilities.

sources.title: Anthropic targets vulnerability detection gains with Claude Security public beta — here's what users can expect
